title: DOJ junks obstruction of justice complaint vs. Atong Ang's lawyer, others
summary: The Department of Justice"s (DOJ) panel of prosecutors has dismissed the obstruction of justice complaint filed against Charlie “Atong” Ang"s lawyer Caroline Cruz and three others for lack of…

blocks.text: The Department of Justice’s (DOJ) panel of prosecutors has dismissed the obstruction of justice complaint filed against Charlie “Atong” Ang’s lawyer Caroline Cruz and three others for lack of evidence, DOJ spokesperson Atty. Polo Martinez confirmed on Tuesday.
“This case has since been dismissed by the DOJ’s panel of prosecutors upon the finding na kulang pa ‘yung ebidensya to charge her currently in court,” Martinez said in an ambush interview.
(This case has since been dismissed by the DOJ’s panel of prosecutors upon the finding that the evidence is still insufficient to charge her currently in court.)

In May, families of missing sabungeros or cockfight enthusiasts filed the complaint against Cruz and three other individuals for allegedly offering cash to their group in exchange for not attending trial hearings.
Charlene Lasco, a sister of missing sabungero Ricardo Lasco, alleged that some would receive P20,000 or P40,000 every month if they agree with the terms.
Meanwhile, Diane Loyola, the wife of one of the missing sabungeros, said the cases are being affected by the absences.
In a report by GMA News in September, only one complainant is left attending the hearings for the missing sabungeros case after other families were allegedly paid off.
Ang remains at large. He is among the subjects of four arrest warrants issued by the Regional Trial Courts of Sta. Cruz, Laguna; Lipa, Batangas; San Pablo, Laguna; and Manila. —NB, GMA News
